summary:
ASTRAEA is an interactive, web-based space mission design and flight simulator developed to bridge the gap between theoretical classroom learning and real-world aerospace systems engineering. Designing a space mission requires balancing competing physical and fiscal demands—scientific instruments, orbital mechanics, power generation, structural mass, telecommunications link budgets, launch vehicle capacities, and cost ceilings. In traditional education, these trade-offs remain isolated in theoretical spreadsheets.

ASTRAEA solves this challenge through Dynamic Closed-Loop Multi-Domain Coupling: any engineering modification (such as adding a high-power radar) instantaneously cascades across mass margins, orbital eclipse battery discharge, data downlink queues, and budget reserves using authentic physics equations (Tsiolkovsky ΔV, inverse-square solar flux, and Friis path loss). Supporting both single-player and 4-Crew Collaborative Team Mode (Flight Director, Systems Engineer, Science Lead, Comms Lead), ASTRAEA guides participants through the complete NASA mission life cycle—from Phase A concept definition and Flight Readiness Reviews (FRR) to real-time orbital simulation, in-flight anomaly resolution, and automated letter-graded post-mission diagnostics.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

ASTRAEA allows students and aspiring engineers to design, manage, and simulate a complete space mission from concept to operation while navigating realistic engineering trade-offs:

- Mission Architecture Selection: Choose from 6 authentic NASA mission scenarios (Earth Cryosphere Sentinel, Artemis Lunar Ice Prospector, Mars Astrobiology Orbiter, Europa Sub-Ocean Explorer, Origins L2 Space Telescope, Asteroid Sample Scout) or an Open Sandbox.

- Subsystem Engineering: Configure the spacecraft bus, power generation (GaAs solar arrays, roll-out ROSA blankets, nuclear MMRTGs), energy storage batteries (Wh), propulsion systems (Cold Gas, Hydrazine, Bi-propellant, High-Isp Ion Thrusters), ADCS pointing stability (arcsec vs. degrees), thermal/radiation shielding, and communication antennas (S, X, Ka-band, and Optical Lasercom).

- Dynamic Closed-Loop Coupling: Calculations execute in real time using fundamental aerospace formulas: Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation (ΔV), Inverse-Square Solar Irradiance (1/r²), Battery Depth-of-Discharge (DoD) during orbital shadow, and RF Link Budgets to NASA's Deep Space Network (DSN).

- Flight Simulation & Operations: A hardware-accelerated 60 FPS Canvas visualizes orbital traversal, day/night terminators, eclipse shadow cones, and active DSN ground station contact rays. In-flight anomalies (solar storms, reaction wheel friction, DSN weather outages) challenge teams to execute real-time tactical decisions.

- Automated Evaluation: Concludes with an automated NASA letter grade (A+ to F), root-cause diagnostics, systems engineering radar charts, and exportable JSON architecture blueprints.

2. What benefits does it have?

- Eliminates "Siloed" Learning: Students immediately witness the ripple effect—adding a 160 kg radar increases mass, forces a $60M launch vehicle upgrade, spikes eclipse battery DoD past 65%, and fills the solid-state recorder.

- Teaches Aerospace Team Dynamics: Features a 4-Crew Member Collaborative Console dividing responsibilities into Flight Director, Systems Engineer, Science Lead, and Comms Lead with built-in competing priorities, requiring team consensus at the Flight Readiness Review (FRR).

- Actionable Feedback: Replaces binary "Pass/Fail" screens with explainable root-cause engineering diagnostics and commendation badges.

3. What is the intended impact?

ASTRAEA democratizes aerospace systems engineering education. By providing a free, zero-installation, browser-native platform, high schools, universities, and STEM clubs worldwide can experience authentic mission architecture without requiring expensive, high-barrier enterprise licenses (e.g., STK) or high-end gaming hardware.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

- Languages & Framework: React 18, TypeScript (for strict type-safety across physical units: kg, W, km/s, Mbps), and Vite 5.

- Styling & UI/UX: Tailwind CSS with custom deep-space dark theme, glassmorphism panels, and Lucide-React icons.

- Simulation & Rendering: HTML5 2D Canvas API for real-time 60 FPS orbital trajectories, day/night terminators, and DSN downlink rays.

- Audio Synthesis: Native HTML5 Web Audio API (procedural synthesis of rocket rumbles, telemetry pings, and warning alarms with zero MP3 asset overhead).

- Deployment & Hosting: Vercel Global Edge CDN and GitHub Pages via GitHub Actions.

5. How is your project creative?

- Interdisciplinary Gamification: Blends the visual appeal of an aerospace control room with authentic systems engineering rigor.

- Procedural Web Audio: Implements a purely mathematical sound engine using browser oscillators and biquad filters, keeping the entire application under 350 kB.

- Dual-Layer Educational Interface: Simple, color-coded telemetry gauges (Green/Amber/Red) for beginners, backed by an expandable NASA Systems Engineering Flight Manual and formula sandbox for advanced students.

6. What factors did your team consider?

- Environmental Physics: Modeled severe radiation in Jupiter's magnetosphere, cryogenic temperatures in lunar polar craters, 14-minute one-way communication delays to Mars, and constant solar illumination at Sun-Earth L2.

- Chemical Battery Safety: Enforced a strict 65% Depth-of-Discharge (DoD) safety ceiling during eclipse shadow passes to reflect real-world battery cell life degradation.

- Fiscal Constraints: Modeled realistic launch vehicle cost tiers (SmallSat, Medium-Lift, Heavy-Lift, Super-Heavy) and Congressional budget caps.
